- tests/test_review_autofix_review_pipeline_contract.py:9459 | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The assertion string omits the leading tab on the `if` line, so it does not exist in the helper script and the test fails with an AssertionError.
  WHY: In scripts/review_untrusted_sandbox.sh the matching text at lines 185-186 is indented one tab inside `if [ -n "${sandbox_root_reason}" ]; then`, so the actual bytes are `\tif [ "${action}" = cleanup ]; then\n\t\techo "::error::REVIEW_SANDBOX_CLEANUP reason=${sandbox_root_reason}" >&2`. The asserted substring starts with a bare `if` (no leading tab) and therefore never matches the file contents, producing a guaranteed test failure on every run, independent of environment.
- TASK_GAP: Requirement: "The fix must remove the cause and ship a regression test that reproduces the failing condition: it fails on the reported head and passes with the fix. Record in the PR that you ran it both ways."
  Expected change site: PR description or a PR comment reporting the regression test was executed against both the pre-fix and post-fix workflow shapes.
  Evidence of absence: The PR description is only "Automated implementation. Closes https://github.com/shubhodeep1/coding-workflows/issues/6694". The sole PR comment (entry[0], author shubhodeep1) summarizes the change but records no test execution or pass/fail results against the pre-fix ordering. None of the five changed files contains a record that the regression test was exercised against a checkout that reordered `Clean up isolated review workspace` back before `Commit changes` (the failing pre-fix shape) and confirmed it failed there.
  SEVERITY: NIT

  WHY: `read_text()` preserves the tab; the literal substring with no leading tab before `if` is not found, so the test raises an AssertionError. The test that is supposed to pin the fix in place therefore fails on the reported head — which means the editor will see the failure and may either "fix" the test (silently weakening the regression contract) or, if the failure is treated as flaky noise, ship a broken assertion that proves nothing. The issue's "ran it both ways" requirement also depends on the test actually running.

The diff's test asserts the post-fix order via `names.index("Commit changes") < names.index(cleanup_name)`, so the regression contract is structurally in place; only the "ran it both ways" record that the issue explicitly requires is missing.
